'''''Heteranthera reniformis''''' common name '''kidneyleaf mud-plantain''', and '''mud plantain'''; is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Pontederiaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:698080-1 |title= Heteranthera reniformis Ruiz & Pav. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3L7CG |title= Heteranthera reniformis Ruiz & Pav. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref> It is found in North America.<ref name="PLANTS">{{PLANTS |symbol=HERE|taxon=Heteranthera reniformis|access-date=1 April 2021 }}</ref> It is listed as a special concern and believed extirpated in [[Connecticut]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20151023162806/http://www.ct.gov/deep/lib/deep/wildlife/pdf_files/nongame/ETS15.pdf "Connecticut's Endangered, Threatened and Special Concern Species 2015"]. State of Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection Bureau of Natural Resources. Retrieved 17 January 2018. (Note: This list is newer than the one used by plants.usda.gov and is more up-to-date.)</ref> It listed as endangered in [[Illinois]] and [[Ohio]].<ref name="PLANTS"/>

==Native American ethnobotany==
The [[Cherokee]] apply a hot [[poultice]] of the root to inflamed wounds and sores.<ref>Hamel, Paul B. and Mary U. Chiltoskey, 1975, Cherokee Plants and Their Uses -- A 400 Year History, Sylva, N.C. Herald Publishing Co., page 45</ref>
